conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; ma = ema(close, maLength); atr(n) is the n-bar average true range

candidates.name: BullTrendBar
candidates.quote: they would have seen a series of bull trend bars and a strong bull trend.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar is a bull trend bar, closing up with a body that is at least a fraction of its range.
notes: Brooks gives no number; other chapters define the same primitive, merged in dedup.

candidates.name: ConsecutiveBullTrendBarRun
candidates.quote: Once the market starts forming four or more consecutive bull trend bars that are not too large and therefore possibly climactic, traders should buy at least a small position at the market instead of waiting for a pullback.
candidates.description: Context filter: at least minRunBars of the last minRunBars bars are bull trend bars (T11-01).

complexity.reason: window count of a single-bar classification

candidates.name: NotClimacticBarSize
candidates.quote: not too large and therefore possibly climactic
candidates.description: Filter: the most recent bar's range does not exceed a climactic multiple of ATR, so a late entry does not buy an exhaustion bar.

candidates.name: LateMarketEntryAfterTrendRun
candidates.quote: If you look at any chart and think that if you had taken the original entry you would still be holding the swing portion of your trade, then you need to enter at the market.
candidates.description: When a run of consecutive, non-climactic bull trend bars has formed (a clear always-in-like move), enter long even without an original position, mechanized as entering at the next bar's open instead of a market fill mid-bar.
candidates.book_order_type: market order immediately (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: combines two window/ATR tests already defined; no new cross-bar state beyond them

notes: The position-sizing half of this idea (trade only the shares you'd still be holding) is rejected below; the engine trades fixed size.

candidates.name: TwoBarReversal
candidates.quote: Bar 2 reversed strongly up and formed a two-bar bull reversal.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a strong trend bar in one direction immediately followed by a strong trend bar in the opposite direction that closes back beyond the first bar's midpoint.
candidates.pseudocode: close[1] < open[1] && (open[1] - close[1]) >= bodyFraction * (high[1] - low[1]) && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && close[0] > (open[1] + close[1]) / 2

candidates.name: InsideBarSignalAfterTwoBarReversal
candidates.quote: The next bar was a bull inside bar and was a good signal bar for the trend from the open bull.
candidates.description: After a two-bar reversal (T11-05), an inside bar is a good with-trend signal bar; buy when a later bar closes above the inside bar's high.
candidates.pseudocode: TwoBarReversal(2) && high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2] && close[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the inside bar high (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: chains fixed-offset bar-pattern tests with no persisted state

candidates.name: TrailStopToLastAddOnSignalBar
candidates.quote: After adding on above bar 6, they could move the stop for the entire position to one tick below the bar 6 signal bar and then trail it up.
candidates.description: Exit: once an add-on has been made above a new with-trend signal bar, ratchet the stop up to just below that bar's low, never lower than the previous stop level.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] < trailStopLevel where trailStopLevel = max(trailStopLevel[1], low[lastSignalBarIndex] - stopTicks * tickSize)
candidates.book_order_type: stop one tick below the most recent signal bar

complexity.reason: a ratcheted (monotonic) stop level is cross-bar state even though each comparison is simple

rejected.quote: you should enter only with the number of shares or contracts that you would still be holding had you taken the original entry, and you should use the same trailing stop.
rejected.reason: position sizing decision, not a bar-level condition; the engine trades fixed size.

rejected.quote: the bar 11 moving average gap bar was also a 20 gap bar pullback. After the first new high following a 20 gap bar pullback, the market usually pulls back and then tests the high again
rejected.reason: chart-specific instance of the '20 gap bar' setup; the general primitive is mined fully in Chapter 17 (T17-08).

rejected.quote: it might be easier emotionally to think of the trade with the open profit as risking someone else's money, that is not the reality... they need to work on this emotional issue.

chapter_summary: Chapter 11 argues that a trader who missed an entry should join a clearly established trend at the market rather than wait for a pullback, sized as if holding only the remaining swing portion of the original trade. It produced a with-trend late-entry rule gated on a run of non-climactic consecutive trend bars, primitives for TwoBarReversal and a reused InsideBar signal bar, and a ratcheted trail-stop-to-last-signal-bar exit. Position sizing and psychology statements were rejected; the chart's '20 gap bar' reference defers to Chapter 17 where that setup is defined.
